ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows 8 black dots around the boundary of a square: there are 3 dots on the top side, 3 dots on the bottom side, and 1 dot at the midpoint position on each of the left and right sides. These dots correspond to points placed at intervals of 1 unit on the boundary of a 2×2 square. Reasoning: Choose any 2 points from the 8 points, without considering order, the total number is C(8,2)=28. The cases where the distance between two points is exactly 1 unit are the pairs of adjacent points along the boundary of the square. Each side length is 2, with 2 segments of unit length; the 4 sides have a total of 4×2=8 such adjacent point pairs. Therefore the probability is 8/28=2/7.
